text: KOSPI tumbled by 6% on Friday, erasing weekly gains amid Trump-Xi Summit and strong foreign outflows

list_items: KOSPI tumbled by 6% on Friday, erasing weekly gains amid the Trump-Xi Summit and strong foreign outflows. The Auto, Insurance and Telecom sectors outperformed this week, while Shipbuilding, Securities and Utilities sectors underperformed the most (Exhibit 9).
■ Foreign investors continued to sell the KOSPI market, driven by outflows for KOSPI Tech and Auto (Exhibit 36).
KOSPI 12m-forward EPS was revised up by +0.1%. The Securities sector saw the strongest upward earnings revisions, while the Utilities sector was revised down the most this week (Exhibit 23).
The KRW weakened 2.6% vs. USD this week. Also, it weakened by 1.4% both vs. JPY and EUR.
The latest Korea Equity Risk Barometer (GSSRKERB Index) is at -0.9, staying in a risk-adverse territory.

text: Charts of the week: Market Concentration and Breadth Pulse Check; MSCI Index Review and Flow Implications (May 2026)

■ Market Concentration and Breadth Pulse Check: Although the KOSPI has risen 78% YTD, only 68 out of 835 listed stocks have outperformed the index, and these names account for nearly 66% of total market

capitalization. This highlights the market's high concentration. Against this backdrop, we see potential opportunities among underperforming stocks, particularly if market breadth begins to improve. While Korea's daily market breadth has remained narrow, it has recently rebounded from below the -1 standard deviation level. In addition, the KOSPI 50 (large-cap index) has outperformed the KOSPI 200 small- and mid-cap segment by more than 2 standard deviations, suggesting potential tactical outperformance opportunities in small- and mid-cap names going forward. Furthermore, despite the overall market rally, nearly $70\%$ of KOSPI-listed stocks are still trading below book value, which we believe presents attractive valuation opportunities. In this context, we highlight stocks trading below book value that are also experiencing positive earnings revisions, as they reflect improving fundamentals despite depressed valuations.

MSCI Index Review and Flow Implications (May 2026): MSCI announced the results of its May 2026 index review after the U.S. market close on May 12, with changes scheduled to take effect after the close on Friday, May 29.
